thread:
maria.l: heads up — customer reported duplicate completions + partial resume after reconnect. They saw the model resume mid-token and then we delivered the full generation again, billed twice. happening intermittently since 17:10 UTC. attaching logs.
ops-chris: ugh. do we have their session token or resume token? any replayable logs?
maria.l: yes. resume_token=rt_9f3b... session_id=sess-1024. logs show SSE disconnect at 17:10:12, client reconnect at 17:10:15 with same resume_token. server accepted resume and then a new full generate started at 17:10:16. here's excerpt from the stream (timestamps removed for brevity):
```
<event>data: {"seq": 23, "chunk": "...partial text...", "resume_token": "rt_9f3b"}
<event>data: {"type": "disconnect", "reason": "network"}
<event>data: {"type": "reconnect_attempt", "resume_token": "rt_9f3b"}
<event>data: {"type": "resume_ack", "resume_token": "rt_9f3b", "last_seq": 23}
<event>data: {"type": "generation_start", "gen_id": "g_abc123"}
<event>data: {"seq": 0, "chunk": "Full generation start..."}
```
maria.l: billing records show two charges for the same user request id. customer sent us a repro via curl.
ashok.k: can you paste the exact curl the customer used? need to verify client behavior.
maria.l: here you go:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-1&stream=true&resume_token=rt_9f3b&request_id=req-555" \
  --data '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":256}'
```
jen_support: note they included `request_id` param but their client reuses resume_token; they do not attach an idempotency header. if server accepts resume blindly we might resume then also enqueue a new generation if the resume path doesn't correctly mark session as active.
ops-chris: plausible. eng-runtime, do we have a race where resume_ack and a concurrent new-generation request both succeed because state flip is not atomic?
eng-runtime-bot: investigating. quick summary of suspected race:
- client reconnects with resume_token
- server validates token and returns resume_ack, but before attaching client socket to existing generation object, a concurrent code path treating the same request as a new generation enqueues a fresh generation job
- both paths produce output; client receives resumed partial + then full new generation => duplicates
ashok.k: two immediate asks: (1) a short-term mitigation to avoid billing/excess work, (2) repro steps so eng can reproduce locally.
jen_support: for mitigation can we reject any new generation requests that include a resume_token header/param while a resume token is still considered live? eg return 409 or a specific 425-like code: `409 ResumeInProgress`.
ops-chris: I like returning 409 with a human-friendly message: "resume in progress; attach idempotency-key to start a fresh generation". also add server-side dedupe: if a resume_token is used and server has last_seq >= 0, check if request_id or idempotency key matches; if absent, prefer resume.
maria.l: customer wants credits; billing-team can we temporarily issue a one-off credit for req-555? they were charged twice.
billing-team: done — credited the duplicate. left note: internal-case-789.
eng-runtime-bot: repro steps for eng:
1) start a long-running generation with model redwood-1 and capture resume_token.
2) simulate network drop (close SSE socket). record last seq N.
3) immediately send a new POST/stream request with the same resume_token but also a fresh `request_id` and no `idempotency-key`.
4) Observe both a resume_ack and a new generation being scheduled in logs. we see two gen_ids.
eng-runtime-bot: local test harness commands:
```
# start server in debug
make dev-run RUNTIME_DEBUG=1

# client script (python) that connects, reads some tokens, then force-closes socket, then spawns a new client that posts with same resume token
python tools/repro/reconnect_dupe.py --model redwood-1 --chunks 5
```
ashok.k: logs we need from customer/infra: full connection trace, request headers for the second POST, and runtime trace showing gen_id creation. also ask them to enable `X-Trace` if they can repro.
maria.l: asked customer for logs + they gave us a HAR with headers. the second request lacked an `Idempotency-Key`. it had `request_id=req-555` only.
ops-chris: patch idea for runtime (short-term hotfix): when a resume_token is presented, atomically claim the resume token by switching token state from "dangling" to "attached:<socketid>" before returning resume_ack. only if atomic claim fails, return 409. currently token state flips in two steps which allows interleaving.
eng-runtime-bot: agreed. implementing: change resume flow to use a compare-and-set on token metadata in the datastore. fallback policy: if CAS fails, return 409 + include `existing_socket` meta in body.
ashok.k: also add server-side billing guard: don't create billing event until generation transitions to "actively_streaming". meaning if both resume and new gen attempted, we will only bill the first one that actually streams tokens to client. implement idempotent billing records keyed by (session_id, request_id, resume_token).
jen_support: can we also add guidance for customers: always include an `Idempotency-Key` for new generation attempts. include example snippet in support KB.
maria.l: wrote KB draft:
"Best practices for reconnects: include resume_token for client reconnects; if you intentionally start a new generation after a disconnect, include `Idempotency-Key` and omit resume_token. If you include both, server will prefer resume and may return 409 if resume is in-flight."
ops-chris: ok, action items:
- eng-runtime: implement CAS-based resume claim + 409 on fail (P0) — patch PR by EOD.
- eng-runtime: hold billing event until stream state confirmed (P1).
- support: notify customer and confirm credit (maria).
- docs/devex: publish KB and add examples to streaming guide (jen).
maria.l: customer accepted credit and flagged as resolved for now but wants root cause and fix timeline. I've told them eng will follow up.
eng-runtime-bot: creating ticket: RUNTIME-1192 "race on resume_token claim causing duplicate gens". adding logs and HAR from customer. assigning to @ashok.k.
ashok.k: taking RUNTIME-1192. will start with CAS proof-of-concept and run repro harness. assigning to self for patch; will ping if we need longer rollback.
jen_support: closing loop with customer in 24h unless they can repro again. leaving thread open for updates.
maria.l: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
